bib.title: Chapter 5: Hardening the Context Engine | Context Engineering for Multi-Agent Systems

question: How do you turn a notebook prototype of a planner-driven multi-agent Context Engine into a modular, logged, dependency-injected pre-production code base?
contributions: Walk-through of the engine in four phases (Initiation, Planning, Execution, Finalization)
Hardened helpers, agents, registry and engine with dependency injection, logging and try/except
Split of the notebook into helpers.py, agents.py, registry.py, engine.py plus a control-deck notebook
Two live runs (standard and two-stage rewrite) with execution trace

limits: No tests, evals, quality metrics, cost or token measurements: the only measurements are two wall-clock durations from single runs.
count_tokens is introduced but not used for budgeting; 'automatically summarizing context' is deferred.
Errors are logged and re-raised, which halts the plan; there is no recovery or fallback beyond retries, yet the summary calls it 'fault-tolerant'.
Described as pre-production only; no deployment, monitoring or security hardening.
Code is abbreviated with elisions (planner, ExecutionTrace, context_engine bodies are not shown).
Authors and book title are not printed in the text; chapter depends on OpenAI (gpt-5), Pinecone and Colab.
practices: Replace print() with Python's logging module at INFO/WARNING/ERROR levels so logs are timestamped and machine-readable (p6).
Inject clients, model names and namespaces as function arguments instead of globals, to enable testing and swapping providers (p6).
Wrap LLM and embedding calls in retry with random exponential backoff, log the specific API error, then re-raise so the orchestrator can halt (p7-8).
Give agents a stable output contract (dict with a fixed key) and make consumers accept both dict and raw string (p10-14).
Keep an ExecutionTrace 'flight recorder' logging plan, each step's agent, inputs, outputs, status and duration (p2-4).
Measure prompt tokens with tiktoken before sending, as a fuel gauge for cost and context-window failures (p6).
Centralise install and client setup in one utils module; keep the notebook as a thin control deck with a config dict (p5, p25).
Keep presentation (execute_and_display) out of the engine library (p19).

terms.definition: Replacing placeholders like $$STEP_1_OUTPUT$$ in a step's inputs with the stored output of an earlier step (resolve_dependencies).
a practice where a function's dependencies are "injected" as arguments
The engine's 'flight recorder' logging every action for transparency and debugging.
Toolkit that describes agents to the Planner (get_capabilities_description) and returns injected handlers to the Executor (get_handler).
